rejected.s: Which dishes hold the soup and rice?
rejected.reason: reader flag two_fit (boxes also fits: 'Which boxes hold the soup and rice?' makes sense, so I can't tell whether the gap needs boxes or dishes.); re-judge: The flag is correct. 'Which boxes hold the soup and rice?' also makes sense. Takeaway or delivery boxes often hold tubs of soup and rice, and lunch boxes hold rice. The sentence gives no clue that only dishes fit, so a child cannot tell which word the gap needs.

rejected.s: Foxes live in dens in the woods.
rejected.reason: reader flag two_fit (Both "they" and "foxes" fit the gap: "They live in dens in the woods" and "Foxes live in dens in the woods" both make sense.); re-judge: The flag is correct. The gap is at the start of the sentence and is followed by 'live', so any plural subject from the bank fits. 'They live in dens in the woods' and 'Foxes live in dens in the woods' are both grammatical and make sense, and 'You live in dens in the woods' also works. Nothing in the sentence points only to 'foxes', so it has more than one right answer and should be dropped.
